title: Getting to Know Him
text: “Well…”
The healer replied, looking slightly intimidated.
“This plague is well-known to originate from the carcasses of dragons. It has been confirmed at our clinic in the past.”
“Are there any unknown factors?”
“None.”
“So that’s how it is. Oh, so now you’re going to suspect the healer?”
“Holy One of the Divine Bird! Please calm your anger!”
The village representative is pleading with my Father as if clinging to a straw. But they really are a despicable bunch. They blame everything on others. It’s no wonder Father is angry.
“It’s easy to blame someone else. But I want you to realize that this time, it’s a problem you yourselves have caused. Honestly, I’m getting sick of it.”
“Haa…” Father let out a deep sigh before sending his Assistant over to the carriage.
“It’s neither God nor the devil—it’s a man-made disaster. This incident, I mean.”
Muttering that, the villagers watched in silence as Father worked silently on the treatments. Eventually, one by one, they clasped their hands in prayer and began to murmur words of repentance.
After that, he devoted himself to treating the patients for a while. Of course, I, Motoyasu, helped Father with the treatments as well.
“Bro, is that about it?”
“Yeah, everyone did a great job.”
After confirming that the symptoms of those suffering from the illness had improved, Father stepped out of the facility and looked toward the mountains.
“Well then, now we’ll go deal with the source of this.”
“Are you, the Saints, going to handle it!?”
“That’s why I came. As long as that thing remains in the mountains, the plague will never subside. To buy the breathing room you asked for… we’ll have to go.”
The villagers bowed their heads as if prostrating themselves.

“Ah… I’ll make this clear first. The revenue earned from turning this into a tourist destination, and the money obtained from selling the dragon’s treasure… make sure you use all of it properly to improve the environment. Under no circumstances should you waste it on foolish things.”
Right before setting off, my Father glared sharply at the villagers.
“Y-yes! Then, as for the reward for the Holy Ones…”
“I’m sorry, but I don’t want it. The village should use that money—not just for itself, but for the mountain’s recovery.”
“O-okay.”
“If things haven’t changed by the time I come back, I won’t set foot here again. You all need to sit down and discuss what to do moving forward.”
With that, Father climbed into the carriage, and we set off for the mountains.
“Well then… I feel like I might have lectured them a bit too much, but if that doesn’t work, I’m at my wit’s end.”
“My brother looked super grumpy, didn’t he?”
“I mean, it’s only natural. They ignored my warnings time and time again, let the plague spread, and then tried to pin it on Ren or shift the blame onto Wyndia-chan, didn’t they?”
“Those people are pretty incredible in a way, aren’t they?”
“Indeed. Filth must be disinfected. Shall I use Magic to wipe them out right now?”
“Motoyasu-kun, are you actually strong enough to pull something like that off?”
“I don’t think it’s impossible. For a village of that size, I think a ‘Liberation Firestorm X’ would wipe it out without a trace.”
“Huh!? Please, don’t do that.”
“Boo…”
“Killing everyone and stealing their treasure… That’s just robbery, isn’t it? Seriously…”
My father muttered in exasperation. Just like the Lazy Pig he is. What he says is pure villainy.
Just as we were talking, the assistant looked down and grabbed the hem of Father’s cloak. Father gave a slightly sad smile and spoke to the assistant.

“Next, we’ll take care of your father… bury him. Since he’s the source of all this contamination, a simple burial might not be enough. In that case, I think we’ll have Motoyasu cremate him or dispose of him using a holy weapon.”
“…Yeah.”
“Gau!”

The monster let out a cry as it followed the carriage, as if to encourage the Assistant. Come to think of it, where had it been all this time? Ah, it had been keeping watch to make sure my Father didn’t get too close to town. Since it couldn’t ride in the carriage, it had been waiting out of sight to avoid attracting attention.
“Well then, it’s going to be tough, but let’s start climbing the mountain.”
“Sakura will do her best.”
“I’ll do my part, too.”
“We’ll be the ones to drive these monsters away.”

Yuki and Kou, who are pulling the carriage, are knocking aside any monsters that look like they might be poisonous as they approach. Let’s leave the material collection to Luna. It seems there are some monsters that have mutated due to the miasma, so these might be rare materials. At the very least, there appear to be some materials I haven’t unlocked yet. At times like this, it really helps to have plenty of Filolial-sama around.
“Gau!”
With a whoosh, the monster breathes fire and incinerates them. Father has cast a barrier, allowing us to climb the mountain fairly quickly.
“In just two weeks, there’s hardly a trace left… It’s scary to just leave a dragon’s carcass lying around, isn’t it…”
“They’re contaminated creatures, aren’t they?”
“Aren’t they basically just a mass of Magic elements to begin with? Like… maybe we just don’t know the details.”
“I have absolutely no interest in dragon ecology.”
“…Motoyasu, you might think you don’t want to know anything about dragons because you hate them, but if you keep that up, you’ll get tripped up.”
“What do you mean by that?”

“You’re from Japan too, so you should understand, right? ‘Know your enemy and know yourself, and you will never be defeated in a hundred battles.’ There’s a big difference in how you handle a situation depending on whether you know your enemy’s nature or not, isn’t there?　If you love Filolial-sama so much, Motoyasu, I think it would be to your advantage to know about dragons—who are Filolial-sama’s rivals.”

Good heavens! You’re absolutely right. Since Filolial-sama detests them, I thought it was best for me to know nothing about them, but if I don’t understand how dragons behave and what they do to torment Filolial-sama, my precious Filolial-sama might end up in serious trouble someday. By learning what kind of creatures dragons are, I’ll be able to deepen my love for Filolial-sama even further.
“Whoa! The guy with the spear just started crying like a waterfall! That’s gross.”
“Just leave him alone. Wyndia, do you know anything about dragons?”
“…… Enough to know that they can marry any kind of creature, how long it takes them to reach adulthood, and how to cast Magic spells.”
“It sounds like there’s still a lot you don’t know. Learning more might help you understand your dad better.”
“……Yeah. I want to know.”
“Speaking of which, the Doctor seemed to know quite a bit about that.”
“Huh? The Doctor… I think that’s the doctor-like person who taught Wyndia-chan all sorts of things in the future, right?”
“That’s right. Besides being Filo-tan’s Doctor—and Filolial-sama, of course—he seemed to have quite a bit of knowledge about dragons as well.”
“Huh… What was his name? Do you know where he came from?”

The Doctor’s name…? I can’t quite recall. I only remember him as the “Doctor.” I think he was already there by the time I arrived at Father’s village. To be honest, I don’t really have much experience talking to him. Naturally, I don’t even know where he was from or what he used to do.
“I have absolutely no idea. I think he just mentioned something about being a ‘genius alchemist’ himself.”
“Whoa… I shouldn’t have asked Motoyasu-kun. If we ever end up looping back, you’d better make sure to remember this properly.”
“Understood.”
“Hmm… If Wyndia-chan were to become Doctor’s apprentice, she might learn even more about monsters.”
“Yeah, I want to learn more.”

I, too, would like to know a little more about Filolial-sama and our arch-enemy, the dragon. Then we’ll find their weaknesses and strike at them. As we chatted like this, we steadily made our way toward the location of the dragon’s corpse.
“Ugh…”
“That’s gross!”
“Ugh…”

My father’s words were spot on. A swarm of monsters called Poison Flies was swarming all over the giant dragon’s corpse. I could tell what it had looked like, but the Poison Flies swarming the rotting flesh made it impossible to see its form at all.
“Honestly, with so many swarming it like this, it’s gross… isn’t it? I’m not really a fan of bugs, but with the smell and everything, this is pretty rough.”
“Dad…”
“Let’s start by wiping out the monsters first.”
“I’ll use Magic to sweep them all away.”
“If we leave it to Motoyasu-kun, he’ll probably burn even the dragon to the bone, won’t he?”
“Oh? Is that a problem?”
My Assistant is clenching his fist tightly.
“Let’s save that as a last resort. First, let’s figure out if we can bury him. Don’t you think Wyndia-chan’s father would want to rest here?”
“Gau!”
Just as the monster roared, the dragon’s carcass began to stir.
“Bro, didn’t that just move?”
The Poisonflies fluttered away with a flutter. Thanks to that, we could now see its entire body.
“It probably just looks like it moved because the gas trapped inside is escaping…”

Father’s words trailed off. The dragon, now reduced to nothing but bones and flesh… slowly raised its front legs and began to sit up. The rotting flesh was oozing and writhing, as if trying to reinforce the remaining parts.
“GYAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA!”
The dragon zombie let out a mighty roar as it sat up.
“…Looks like it wasn’t the gas after all.”
